answer.origin: NVIDIA Corporation blog post titled 'NVIDIA Unlocks AI Compute at Scale, Inviting Partners to Power the AI Infrastructure Buildout', published and stated 2026-07-01; it is a company statement, with Sharon AI and Firmus quotes and campus figures relayed through NVIDIA's blog.
answer.note: Source claim: NVIDIA says it is introducing a new business model under which AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure for AI-native, enterprise and ISV customers, with economics aligned through a revenue-sharing and credit-support model. NVIDIA says it would earn both standard product revenue and a share of cloud revenue on supported capacity, which it describes as a recurring, usage-linked earnings stream. Conditional interpretation: if the model is executed as described, NVIDIA's revenue from these deployments would combine hardware sales with a usage-linked share of cloud revenue, and it would also carry credit-support exposure that the source does not quantify. The source gives no revenue-share rate, credit-support size, signed partner count, or timing of revenue, so it supports the existence and structure of the model, not its scale. The Firmus figures (campus expected to scale to 360 megawatts and up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs) are the partner's own plan as relayed by NVIDIA; they are a forward supply and demand indicator for NVIDIA GPUs but not confirmed orders or delivered volumes. The Sharon AI quote is supportive commentary with no quantities. The AI-native customer examples (Baseten, Fireworks AI, Together AI) describe demand conditions and are not evidence of purchases by these companies from NVIDIA or AI clouds.
limitations: The revenue-share percentage, credit-support amount, and accounting treatment of the product-plus-cloud-revenue structure are not disclosed.

It is not stated whether Firmus or Sharon AI have signed agreements under this model, or on what terms; the source describes them as partners and as building DSX AI factories, not as parties with disclosed contracts.
The Firmus 360 MW and 170,000 GPU figures are described as expected scale; the source gives no build schedule, financing status, or completion date.
The source is a company blog and gives no quantified revenue, timing, or capacity commitment attributable to NVIDIA from this model.
follow_up: Check NVIDIA's next quarterly and annual filings for any disclosure of this business model, its revenue recognition, or credit-support obligations.
Check Firmus and Sharon AI public announcements or filings for signed agreements with NVIDIA, financing for the Batam campus, and construction timing.
Check whether the AI-native companies named (Baseten, Fireworks AI, Together AI) disclose NVIDIA capacity arrangements through this model.
